text:
andrea: heads-up — CSMs flagged two customers asking for prescriptive guidance: one wants specific batching guardrails for low-latency tiers, the other wants quantization recommendations tied to quality budgets. Can we sketch launch criteria?

sam: thanks. quick q — do we treat these as two separate mini-features or one 'guidance' workstream in Optimize?

andrea: I lean single workstream with two deliverables: (A) batching + cache guardrails for realtime and high-throughput tiers, (B) quantization recommendations + expected quality delta table. both gated by eval alerts integration.

tyler: +1. must include concrete knobs for engineers (batch_size limits, max_wait_ms, KV cache TTL) and example configs. customers just want copy-paste snippets.

lia: can we add a safety net: a quick A/B fallback policy so if quantization causes >X% drop on evals we auto-fallback to fp16 variant? we already have rollout primitives.

andrea: yes — that's part of launch must-have. propose: ability to declare an 'eval-safety' check that triggers an automated rollback/fallback.

sam: propose launch criteria draft: 1) Docs + 3 example configs (realtime, steady throughput, offline batch). 2) SDK helpers + CLI to apply configs. 3) Eval-triggered alerting wired to console + webhook. 4) Canary fallback automation working end-to-end. 5) Quantization guidance with measured token-cost and eval score delta for at least 2 models.

tyler: timeline? we have pilot customers waiting. realistic: 6 weeks for an MVP if we scope examples and reuse existing rollout infra.

lia: dependencies: need eval infra to support rapid sampling + baseline, and Console work for alert UI. who owns eval infra changes?

andrea: eng-ml to own the quant eval harness; eng-platform picks up SDK/CLI and rollout wiring; product owns examples and acceptance tests.

sam: customer asks included specific SLOs: one wants p99 <120ms for short prompts. Batching guidance should include recommended instance types and expected latency impact per-batch. we should quantify.

tyler: I can prototype a micro-benchmark doc: table with batch sizes vs p50/p95/p99 on g4dn vs a100 (simulated numbers). that will help set expectations in guidance.

lia: for quantization recommendations — include simple matrix: quant level (int8/int4), expected cost reduction %, typical quality hit (BLEU/ROUGE/embedding-sim) with a short note about use-cases where it's acceptable.

andrea: acceptance criteria (customer-facing): 1) Copy-paste config that meets sub-120ms p99 in our internal perf tests for 'realtime' profile; 2) Quant table with measured deltas for two models; 3) Eval-alerts wired and tested with one upstream customer; 4) Docs and a 45-min workshop run with the customer.

sam: can we make the config format small JSON + human-readme. e.g.:

{
  "profile": "realtime",
  "max_batch_size": 8,
  "max_wait_ms": 20,
  "kv_cache_ttl_ms": 60000,
  "fallback_policy": {
    "signal": "eval_safety",
    "threshold_pct": 2,
    "action": "fallback_to:fp16"
  }
}

sam: that's intentionally tiny. engineers can tweak.

tyler: looks good. small suggestion: add recommended quant profile name so ops can pick the quantized artifact: "quant_profile": "int8-aggressive-v1"

lia: about eval-triggered alerts — need to define SLOs for eval sampling frequency, sample size, and what metrics we measure (e.g., embedding distance, token-level perplexity, downstream perf).

andrea: agreed. propose defaults: sample 200 requests/week per route, measure embedding cosine and a route-specific metric (if available). threshold: alert if mean embedding similarity drops by >4% or route metric degrades >3%.

sam: those numbers seem reasonable as starting defaults. customers can opt-in to stricter gates.

tyler: security/compliance note: customers on Private want configs to be deployable via our private control plane and not send traffic to hosted evals. must include local eval harness instructions.

lia: ops-bot: deploy-preview ready?

ops-bot: deploy-preview pipeline for 'optimize-guidance' created — tests will run on PR. :white_check_mark:

andrea: next steps: sam/tyler to draft config examples + perf microbench within 1 week. lia to draft eval sampling defaults and alert thresholds. I'll draft customer acceptance checklist and schedule pilot workshop.

sam: i’ll own the docs snippets and CLI helpers.

tyler: will get a first pass perf table by EOD Friday.

lia: will sync with eng-ml on local eval harness by Tue.

andrea: thanks. if anyone has customer quotes or must-have constraints add them here. otherwise I’ll pull this into a short PRD and a follow-up planning thread. :thumbsup:
